-- Evidence warnings --
  * probe: --probe-screen <TMP>/screen_synthtest.txt; dx=3000; 2 knob verdict(s) parsed
  * this case is not one of the six PHYSICS-GRAY campaign cases physics_templates.json already knows about -- any template needing per-case pairing (P04/P05/P06) used the generic rule (physics.generic_extra_edits) instead of a hand-written entry
  * allowed fidelity labels: WITHIN-FLOOR, SMALL-DRIFT
  * fidelity labels describe the MODEL's OWN drift vs a same-physics twin at a different STRICT decomposition (the chaos floor), not observed forecast skill against any observation/reanalysis -- see decision 0051
  * PHYSICS-GRAY training evidence on hardware_id='hw-train-synthetic': 60 row(s), 6 case(s) (phystrain0, phystrain1, phystrain2, phystrain3, phystrain4, phystrain5)
  * cost-share filter: this case has no profile row in the ledger (profile_{radiation,micro,dynamics,mpi,io}_share all absent) -- no candidate was annotated or demoted. Profile one run of this case to enable it.
  * floor_zero hint: if DECOMP=C13 and TWIN_DECOMP=C06 happen to produce BIT-IDENTICAL output (rms diff 0 on every compared field), the twin's chaos floor is floor_zero -- a real degenerate case fidelity_gate.py handles explicitly, but a candidate's drift cannot be judged against a zero floor. If fidelity_gate.py reports floor_zero for this pair, rerun the twin at a different TWIN_DECOMP (known example: isc21's C02/C06 pair was bit-identical; C13 was used instead).

  infeasible: <failed>/<tried> training cases (every replicate FAILED); OOF-miss: leave-one-case-out out-of-fold dangerous-miss <n>/<total> (predicted allowed, measured LARGE-DRIFT), or insuff(n=<n>) below the 5-prediction floor.

==============================================================================
ACCURACY-FIRST view (--objective accuracy) -- same candidates, ranked by fidelity error
==============================================================================
  fidelity error = nd, the normalized difference from the campaign REFERENCE at the last common time.
  floor_ratio = that drift divided by the chaos floor (the SAME physics re-run at TWIN_DECOMP).
  HARD RULE: floor_ratio <= 1.00 means the candidate moved the solution no more than merely re-decomposing the run does. Such a candidate is reported as indistinguishable from changing the decomposition and is NEVER presented as an accuracy improvement -- chasing error below the chaos floor is meaningless. Measured example from this campaign: pure RK2 (D02) on conus12 at 12 h had floor_ratio 1.593, i.e. dropping an entire RK stage was already within 2x of just re-decomposing.
  Predicted speed is still reported for every candidate: accuracy mode changes the RANKING, not the evidence.

  These are the P/D-series templates: they buy speed and pay in drift, so a SMALLER error is strictly better and rank 1 is the most conservative choice.

-- Accuracy levers (A-series), ranked by LARGEST measurable correction (5) --
  Ranked the OTHER WAY ROUND on purpose. For an A-series template the same nd is not an error, it is the correction the extra work applies to the reference; a small one means the reference was already converged in that knob and the template is pure added cost. Ranking these ascending alongside the cost levers would reward exactly the ones that do nothing.

-- Below the chaos floor: NOT accuracy improvements (1) --
  D02       cost      indistinguishable from changing the decomposition (floor_ratio 0.800 <= 1.00): its drift is at or below the chaos floor, so this is NOT an accuracy improvement

-- Pareto front over (predicted cost, fidelity error) (1) --
  Every operating point that is not beaten on BOTH axes at once. perf-first is the cheapest end of this front and acc-first the lowest-error end; anything between them is a legitimate trade the user can pick. A candidate off the front is strictly worse than something on it.
  P03       cost      error=0.00849135     cost=-32.41% [-32.4,-32.4]  predicted (fidelity regression, this case)
  not placed on the front: D02 (below the chaos floor); D04 (no predicted time-to-solution); D06 (no predicted time-to-solution); D07 (no predicted time-to-solution)

-- Decomposition: a free axis in accuracy mode --
  DECOMP=C13 (this run's own STRICT top-1 shortlist entry) is unchanged from perf mode: STRICT decomposition knobs (nproc_x/nproc_y/numtiles/OMP/distribution) redistribute the same arithmetic and never change the physics, so they are a FREE AXIS in accuracy mode -- the fastest legal decomposition is also the most accurate one. They do set the chaos floor every fidelity number below is judged against, which is the opposite of being a fidelity lever: a decomposition change is the NOISE, not the signal.

-- What to run to verify (accuracy campaign) --
  STAGE 1 -- run the A-series at DECOMP alongside the usual P00 reference and TWIN_DECOMP twin, and gate each A-template against P00. An A-template whose floor_ratio <= 1.00 means P00 was ALREADY converged in that knob: the extra work bought nothing measurable and that template is pure added cost, never an accuracy improvement. STAGE 2 -- for whichever A-template survives with the LARGEST drift (the biggest real correction), re-run fidelity_gate.py using its own wrfout as --reference. Only then is every other candidate's nd an error against a better-converged solution rather than a distance from P00, which is what the accuracy ranking above actually wants to measure. Until stage 2 exists, treat the cost-lever ranking as 'least departure from the current operating point', not as 'most accurate'. The user makes the final decision -- this tool only narrows the search.
  STAGE 1: sbatch --export=ALL,CASE=synthtest,MODE=physics,PCONFIGS=A01+A02+A03+A04+A05,DECOMP=C13,TWIN_DECOMP=C06 campaign/strict_campaign.sbatch
  STAGE 2: python3 fidelity_gate.py --reference <A-TEMPLATE wrfout_d01_*> --twin <TWIN wrfout_d01_*> --candidate <P00 REFERENCE wrfout_d01_*> --family all --out-prefix <out_dir>/fidelity_synthtest_P00_vs_converged
  STAGE 2: then re-run each cost lever's gate the same way, swapping --reference for the A-template's wrfout: D02; P01; P03
